title: Is Social Media Management Worth It for a Malaysian Small Business? DIY vs Done-for-You (2026)
meta_description: Is social media management worth it in Malaysia? Compare DIY hours against a done-for-you package from RM888 to RM2,888 a month, with a simple cost test and red flags to check.
keywords: is social media management worth it
DIY social media small business Malaysia
content:
## Short answer

For most Malaysian small businesses that want to post at least three times a week, social media management is worth it once you price in the owner's own time. A done-for-you package is a cost you can compare directly against hours you would otherwise spend on content, captions, replies and ads. The test is simple: if the work is taking more hours than the owner can spare, outsourcing usually pays back.

## The real cost of doing it yourself

DIY looks free because no invoice arrives. In practice the cost sits in hours. A typical week for a small shop owner includes planning posts, shooting or editing short videos, designing simple graphics, replying to comments and messages, and checking whether boosted posts are doing anything.

As an illustration only, not a client result: if the owner spends 10 hours a week on this work and values their time at RM50 an hour, that is RM2,000 a month of time that never shows up on a bank statement. Add the cost of a poorly made video or a rushed design and the gap widens.

## When DIY still makes sense

Do it yourself if you already enjoy creating content, if you post only once or twice a week, and if sales come mainly from walk-ins rather than online enquiries. A scheduling tool costs very little, and a consistent calendar matters more than a big budget. Our guide on [planning a 30-day content calendar](/blog/plan-30-day-social-media-content-calendar-malaysia-2026) walks through that process step by step.

## When outsourcing is worth it

Outsourcing tends to pay off when three things are true. First, posting has slipped for more than a month. Second, the owner cannot separate creative work from daily operations. Third, you run paid ads and need someone watching them every week, not only when a campaign launches.

## What a fair package includes

Compare providers on deliverables rather than promises. A clear package should state how many short videos, how many designs, which platforms it covers and whether paid ads are optimised. For reference, Cheaper Nexus's social media management package is RM2,888 a month and includes 2 short videos, 5 professional designs, management for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Xiaohongshu, and Meta ad optimisation, with a listed original value of RM5,738. If you want to test the work first, the first-experience package is RM888 a month, once per company, with 1 short video, 2 designs and basic Meta ad setup.

## Red flags before you sign

- No sample work you can open and judge
- Vague promises such as reach or follower targets with no deliverable list
- Long lock-in terms before you have seen one month of output
- Ad budgets charged through the agency with no transparent reporting
- Case studies with no named business and no verifiable numbers

If a provider cannot show real past work, treat that as a warning sign rather than a minor detail.

## How to decide this month

Write down the hours you spent on marketing last month, then the number of posts that went live. If the hours are high and the posts are few, outsourcing is probably worth a trial. Start with a short contract, agree on what success looks like for the first 30 days, and review the output together.

topic: Social media management cost-benefit for Malaysian SMEs

faq.q: How much does social media management cost in Malaysia?
faq.a: Cheaper Nexus lists its social media management package at RM2,888 a month, which covers 2 short videos, 5 designs, management for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Xiaohongshu, and Meta ad optimisation. A lighter first-experience package is RM888 a month, offered once per company.

faq.q: How do I know if I have enough time to manage social media myself?
faq.a: Track your marketing hours for two weeks, including planning, creating, replying and checking ads. If you consistently spend more than about 10 hours a week and posts still go out irregularly, the work is probably better outsourced.

faq.q: Is a first-month trial package a good way to test an agency?
faq.a: Yes, if the trial shows real deliverables you can judge. Check the video quality, the design files you receive and whether ad setup is explained clearly. A RM888 trial with 1 short video and 2 designs is enough to see whether the working style suits you.

faq.q: Should a small business pay for social media management or hire a full-time staff member?
faq.a: A full-time hire usually costs more than a package once salary, EPF and training are included. A package suits a business that needs steady output across several platforms, while a staff member makes more sense only when the daily workload justifies a full role.

faq.q: What should I check before signing a social media management contract?
faq.a: Confirm the number of videos and designs per month, the platforms covered, who owns the final files, how ad budgets are handled and the notice period for cancelling. A clear written scope of 2 videos and 5 designs per month is far more useful than a general promise of growth.
